subject.title: [Security] Plaintext credential leakage in diagnostic crash dumps

question: Does a privately generated current-main diagnostic export retain a synthetic credential inside an escaped or stringified structure, and which canonical sanitizer should own the defense?
rationale: The public report alleges credential disclosure but lacks a safe artifact-level reproduction, while choosing between text normalization, structured sanitization, or both affects a security boundary and false-negative risk.

options.title: Private canary reproduction
options.body: Run the real export with synthetic secrets in representative encoded structures, identify the exact leaking archive entry, and patch the owning diagnostic sanitizer.

options.title: Defense-in-depth hardening
options.body: Add bounded escaped-structure handling to both diagnostic text and structured sanitizers after reviewing denial-of-service and over-redaction risks.

options.title: Close after negative proof
options.body: Close only if a comprehensive current-main canary matrix proves that all reported structures are already removed from the final archive.

recommendation.title: Private canary reproduction
recommendation.body: Run the real export with synthetic secrets in representative encoded structures, identify the exact leaking archive entry, and patch the owning diagnostic sanitizer.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a protected core security-boundary decision requiring authority to coordinate private reproduction and disclosure-safe handling.
